question: Why did the biochar catalyst keep the glycerol carbonate yield above 90% over four reuse cycles?
expect: premise false: the yield declined progressively to 72.04% by the fourth reuse, attributed to potassium leaching (about 50% K loss, basicity 3.66 to 2.00 mmol/g) (sec. 3.8)
rendered:
Waste-derived mesoporous biochar for glycerol to glycerol carbonate upgrading: intensified process design and techno-economic analysis 

The biochar catalyst kept the glycerol carbonate yield above 90% over four reuse cycles because the catalyst retained its structural integrity and alkaline properties, despite a slight decrease in potassium content and basic site density. The catalyst's mesoporous structure and potassium-enriched composition allowed it to maintain its catalytic efficiency, even after multiple reuse cycles.
